change.author: CarinaWolli

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects a slot that falls outside any one of the day's ranges, not outside all of them
findings.body: `workingHours.find(...)` returns true (meaning "unavailable") as soon as one entry covering `slotStartTime.day()` does not contain the slot. A user can have several entries on the same UTC day, and `getWorkingHours` (packages/lib/availability.ts:76-124) creates one entry per availability row. It also adds an overflow entry on the next or previous day when hours cross UTC midnight (availability.ts:103-121). Take an organizer in America/Los_Angeles working Mon–Fri 9–17. That gives `[1020–1439]` on Mon–Fri plus `[0–60]` on Tue–Sat. A Tuesday 18:00 UTC slot falls outside `[0–60]` and is rejected, and a Tuesday 00:30 UTC slot falls outside `[1020–1439]` and is rejected too. So every weekday slot for that host disappears, and no error explains why. A split day such as 9–12 plus 13–17 breaks the same way. This now runs for every fixed host (line 488) and every round-robin host (line 513), because both spread `workingHours` from `userAvailability`. Reject the slot only when no matching entry contains it, e.g. `workingHours.some(wh => wh.days.includes(day) && start >= wh.startTime && end <= wh.endTime)`, applied only when the user has an entry for that day.

findings.title: A date with two or more override ranges blocks every slot on that date
findings.body: `dateOverrides.find` returns true (unavailable) for any override on the slot's date whose range does not contain the slot. A user can set several time ranges for one override date, and `getUserAvailability` (packages/core/getUserAvailability.ts:215-224) creates one entry per range. With ranges 09–12 and 14–17, a 10:00 slot is "before" the 14–17 range (line 118), and a 15:00 slot is "after" the 09–12 range (line 123). So both are rejected and the host shows no availability that day. Collect the overrides for the slot's date first, then reject only if the slot fits inside none of them.

findings.title: Working-hours `end` is computed from the slot start, so slots that run past the end of working hours pass
findings.body: `end` is `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, the same value as `start`. For hours ending at 17:00, a 60-minute slot at 16:30 passes `end > workingHour.endTime`. For round-robin hosts, `getSlots` builds slots from everyone's combined hours, so another host's later hours can produce that 16:30 slot, and it then gets assigned to this host. Use `slotEndTime` here.

findings.title: Override bounds check accepts slots that only partly overlap the override
findings.body: A slot is rejected only if it ends at or before the override start (lines 117-121), or starts strictly after the override end (line 123). So with an override of 09:00–12:00, a 60-minute slot at 08:30 or at 11:30 counts as available. A slot starting exactly at 12:00 also passes, because `isAfter` is strict. For round-robin hosts these slots can come from other hosts' availability (see `buildSlots` in packages/lib/slots.ts:85-100). The check should require `slotStartTime >= start && slotEndTime <= end`.

findings.title: `===` between two Dayjs objects is always false, so the start == end check never runs
findings.body: `dayjs(...).add(...) === dayjs(...).add(...)` compares two newly created object references, which are never identical. The branch is meant for an override with no available time (start equals end), and it can never be reached. In that case a slot starting exactly at the override instant passes both later checks: it does not end before the start, and it does not start after the end. Such a slot is then accepted through `dateOverrideExist`. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `.valueOf()`.

findings.title: Override date is matched on the UTC calendar date, not the organizer's date
findings.body: Lines 107-110 shift the override start to real UTC and compare its `YYYY MM DD` with the slot's UTC date. For organizers far from UTC, the override's local day spans two UTC dates. Example: a Los Angeles override on the 13th, 09:00–17:00 PST, is 17:00 on the 13th to 01:00 on the 14th UTC. Then (a) the 12th's 16:00–17:00 PST working-hour slots (00:00–01:00 UTC on the 13th) match the override date and are rejected as "before the override". (b) The override's own slots after 16:00 PST fall on the 14th UTC, so the override is ignored for them and they go through the working-hours path. Also, `dayjs(date.start).format()` formats in the server's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` is UTC. Compare both dates in `organizerTimeZone`, e.g. `slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone).format("YYYY-MM-DD")` against `dayjs.utc(date.start).format("YYYY-MM-DD")` (the stored wall-clock date).

findings.title: Converted override minutes wrap at midnight, so overrides that cross the invitee's midnight are dropped or shown on the wrong day
findings.body: `startTime`/`endTime` are taken as `hour()*60+minute()` after adding the offset, so they wrap modulo 24h. But `activeOverrides` (line 206-208) still picks the override for the invitee day equal to the organizer's date, without the offset. Example: organizer in UTC with an override of 17:00–23:00, invitee at +5:30. The result is start=1350 and end=270, which `buildSlots` skips as invalid (line 68). Every slot of that override is lost. Example two: an override of 20:00–23:00 becomes 01:30–04:30. It is shown at 01:30 on the organizer's date, a day before the real time. Both start and end need to be shifted as instants, and the override assigned to the invitee day the shifted times fall on.

findings.title: New test does not exercise the new availability checks
findings.body: The only added case uses an IST schedule (03:30–11:30 UTC, which doesn't cross UTC midnight), a single override range, and a single fixed host. That is why it misses the defects above. Consider adding cases for: an organizer whose hours cross UTC midnight (e.g. America/Los_Angeles 9–17), a day with two working-hour ranges, an override date with two ranges, and a round-robin event with a date override, which the PR title targets.

contracts.action: checkIfIsAvailable now filters slots by per-user date overrides and working hours
contracts.equivalent_path: getSlots in packages/lib/slots.ts already applies working hours and overrides when building the candidate slots
contracts.before_after: Before, checkIfIsAvailable only checked busy times and seats. Now, for fixed hosts (line 488) and round-robin hosts (line 513), it also rejects slots outside that user's overrides or working hours. Working hours come from getWorkingHours, in UTC minutes, with overflow entries when hours cross midnight.
contracts.visible_effect: Rejected slots are left out of availableTimeSlots and never reach the booker's time list. When every slot is rejected, the day shows as unavailable, with no error.
contracts.failure_mode: Synchronous. A wrong result fails silently as missing slots: no log and no error.

contracts.action: getSlots converts override wall-clock minutes from organizer to invitee timezone
contracts.equivalent_path: Working hours are localised through getWorkingHours with the invitee's utcOffset (packages/lib/slots.ts:170-176)
contracts.before_after: Before, the organizer's wall-clock minutes were used directly. Now they are shifted by the invitee-minus-organizer offset, but the result wraps modulo 24h, and the activeOverrides day selection is unchanged.
contracts.visible_effect: Override slots appear at the invitee's local time. When the converted range crosses midnight, they are dropped or shown on the wrong day.

summary:
This PR adds date-override and working-hours checks to `checkIfIsAvailable`, and converts override times to the invitee's timezone in `getSlots`. The new checks are wrong in ways that hide availability with no error. Two are blockers:
- **Working hours:** a slot is rejected if any one of the day's entries excludes it. Every organizer whose hours cross UTC midnight (e.g. US Pacific 9–5) loses all weekday slots, and so does anyone with a split day.
- **Date overrides:** a date with several override ranges loses all its slots.

Smaller fixes:
- The working-hours `end` is computed from the slot start.
- The override bounds check accepts slots that only partly overlap the override.
- `===` between two Dayjs objects is always false, so the start == end check is dead.
- Override dates are matched on the UTC date instead of the organizer's date.
- Converted override minutes wrap at midnight in `getSlots`, which drops slots or shows them a day early.

The added test only covers an IST single-range case and misses all of these.
